markdown_report:
The strongest next experiment is **gradually introduced, bounded negative weighting within corrected BERT4Rec**. At 30% progress, this offers a smaller, more interpretable intervention than adding text or temporal attention.

Three starting insights guide the proposal. First, Electronics has 11.89% negative-over-positive training conflicts and a negative tenth-percentile margin; these establish a discrimination problem on inspected training targets, not held-out failure. Second, user feedback distinguishes broad relevance from specific usefulness; stronger contextual competition could help, but cannot establish ownership or compatibility. Third, diagnostic coverage now exists in every category, superseding earlier zero-coverage observations; deployment parity and consumed-record provenance remain unavailable.

Three literature insights organize the alternatives. Hard-BPR motivates caution around uncertain hard negatives, without identifying false negatives here. R²NS motivates delaying hardness interventions, although its results do not establish BERT4Rec gains. NOVA-BERT motivates keeping item identity separate from attention-guiding side information; its findings do not validate a scratch-trained text adaptation.

| Direction | Atomic proposal | Evidence and gap |
|---|---|---|
| Optimization | Bounded weighting of existing K=16 negatives | Minimal change; contextual benefits unverified |
| Semantic specificity | Joint scratch-trained title guidance in attention | NOVA-BERT; requires complete target-text masking |
| Temporal relevance | Near-zero-initialized time-gap attention bias | TiSASRec; omitted sensitivity results establish no preferred recency direction |

Scores below use O/P/U/M/D for originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bounded weighting | 3/7/6/8/3 | O: clean combination; P: extensible; U: contextual discrimination; M: targets conflicts; D: local change | O: established components; P: uncertain transfer; U: indirect; M: training exposure; D: controls require care |
| Title attention guidance | 5/8/8/6/7 | O: constrained adaptation; P: semantic extensibility; U: specific cues; M: richer distinctions; D: one network | O: prior art; P: sparse text supervision; U: missing specifications; M: no measured text deficit; D: writer changes |
| Time-gap bias | 4/7/8/5/6 | O: BERT adaptation; P: temporal learning; U: current intent; M: contextual separation; D: small parameter count | O: established mechanism; P: sparse timestamps; U: recency assumptions; M: sensitivity evidence omitted; D: timestamp routing |

Select bounded weighting. It explicitly targets **loosely related items displacing specific matches** and **specialized equipment receiving support without sufficient contextual evidence**, through stronger competition against moderately challenging candidates. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated remedies. It also targets Electronics’ measured ranking conflicts.

Warm up uniformly, then gradually introduce detached, bounded weights normalized within each target. Preserve candidates and masking. Weighted candidate cross-entropy changes both relative gradient allocation and aggregate pressure; normalization does not isolate either effect. Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve one model per category, all benchmark constraints and appended-mask inference.

idea.description: Test a warm-start curriculum of bounded, detached hardness weights on the same 16 uniformly sampled negatives in the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Keep one independently trained network/checkpoint per category. Change only the masked-target candidate-ranking loss; preserve architecture, corruption, terminal-mask allocation, sampling eligibility and inference.
idea.motivation: Electronics has 181 negative-over-positive conflicts among 1,522 inspected training targets (11.89%) and a tenth-percentile margin of -0.2245. This supports investigating contextual discrimination, without establishing false negatives or held-out failure. The user-facing hypotheses are that moderately challenging competitors help reduce loosely related recommendations displacing specific matches and unsupported specialized equipment receiving high ranks. Neither outcome is guaranteed, and interaction supervision cannot certify compatibility, ownership or immediate need. Current diagnostics already inspected ten batches per category; instrumentation should preserve this measured coverage rather than claim to restore missing coverage.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is integration code for the supplied baseline, whose source is absent from the prompt, not an executable replacement train.py. Audit the actual baseline objective before applying it. The proposed control is uniform candidate CE/K=16; do not silently describe an objective change from another baseline loss as a weighting-only intervention.

For each target, let d_j = negative_logit_j - positive_logit. Define detached hardness h_j = sigmoid(d_j), raw weights r_j = 1 + alpha*h_j, and normalized weights w_j = 16*r_j/sum(r). With alpha in [0,1], weights are positive, average one and bounded between 0.5 and 2. Use L = log(1 + sum_j w_j*exp(d_j)). No logQ correction or full-softmax equivalence is claimed. Detachment gives a semi-gradient update: it does not differentiate the complete score-dependent weighting function. Increasing weights saturate rather than declining for extremely hard negatives; uncertain hard candidates remain a risk.

Use E=min(int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS','200')),200), requiring E>=1, and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Warm up for ceil(0.2*E) epochs, then increase alpha linearly to one over the remaining declared epochs. If none remain, retain uniform weights. Keep the schedule tied to declared epochs and log the selected checkpoint's realized exposure. The numeric choices are proposed settings, not validated optima.

Keep the same K=16 uniform candidate draws, replacement policy, exclusions and across-target reduction as the audited uniform control. Retain repeated-ID multiplicities. Use training information only for eligibility. Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; purpose-separated RNG streams should keep users, crops, masks and candidates matched across new controls. Introducing RNG isolation changes an existing shared-stream implementation, so distinguish matched controls from the unchanged host anchor.

The minimum new comparison, if the host budget permits, is uniform CE/K=16 versus scheduled weighted CE/K=16. Independent comparison models are never combined or reused as initializations. An optional immediate-weighting control tests schedule dependence. Fixed weight sums do not fix gradient norms or negative-gradient mass. Log realized weights, ranking conflicts, sparse positive/negative logit-gradient summaries and clipping frequency; parameter-gradient measurements require explicit measurement and must not be inferred from logit gradients. All trials, diagnostics and failures consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Prioritize complete four-category configurations before optional controls.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, supplied splits, single-GPU execution and all four routes: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep the existing embedded predictor writer consistent with the saved architecture/configuration. Each route loads exactly one selected checkpoint. Construct left_pad(history[-(L-1):]+[MASK], L) and read the greatest nonpadding index. Hide supervised targets from bidirectional inputs; exclude PAD and MASK from candidate recommendations.

Retain family-specific sample_batch and ModelView, view.model as the actual nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Loader tuples remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Multi-negative tensors remain internal to training. Preserve the existing fixed-one-negative diagnostic protocol and report actual inspected coverage. Use independent diagnostic RNG and restore model mode afterward. Unavailable provenance, attention hooks and exported-predictor runners remain unavailable; do not replace them with claimed passes.

Select only through the pinned host macro validation HR@10, with 200 users/category and 99 unique negatives. Report actual per-category and macro results without inventing gains. Training margins are exposure-dependent and scale-sensitive; the conflict rate complements them. Omitted history-sensitivity outcomes establish no recency conclusion. No independent popularity/transition scores, ensembles, pretrained weights, unavailable metadata or hidden test information enter this experiment.
idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch


def weighting_strength(epoch, maximum_epochs):
    E = min(int(maximum_epochs), 200)
    if E < 1 or not 0 <= epoch < E:
        raise ValueError('Invalid epoch schedule')
    warm = math.ceil(0.2 * E)
    if epoch < warm or warm == E:
        return 0.0
    return (epoch - warm + 1) / (E - warm)


def bounded_masked_candidate_loss(positive_logits, negative_logits, alpha):
    """Returns per-target losses; preserve baseline aggregation externally."""
    if not 0.0 <= alpha <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError('alpha must be in [0, 1]')
    positive_logits = positive_logits.reshape(-1)
    if negative_logits.shape != (positive_logits.numel(), 16):
        raise ValueError('Expected exactly 16 negatives per target')
    if positive_logits.numel() == 0:
        raise ValueError('Caller must skip/count empty supervised batches')

    # FP32 loss arithmetic; gradients still flow to original model logits.
    differences = negative_logits.float() - positive_logits.float()[:, None]
    with torch.no_grad():
        raw_weights = 1.0 + alpha * torch.sigmoid(differences.detach())
        weights = raw_weights / raw_weights.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    weighted_differences = differences + weights.log()
    zero = torch.zeros_like(positive_logits.float())[:, None]
    losses = torch.logsumexp(torch.cat([zero, weighted_differences], dim=-1), dim=-1)
    return losses, weights.detach()


# Integration into the supplied corrected BERT4Rec, without changing its APIs:
# E = min(int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')), 200)
# For each of the four supplied categories:
#   Initialize one model with training seed 42.
#   For epoch in range(E):
#     For step in range(200):
#       Obtain baseline masked inputs and labels using unchanged sample_batch.
#       Obtain the same 16 eligible uniform negatives as the matched control.
#       valid = (sequence == MASK) & (positive != PAD)
#       Skip/count batches without valid supervised targets.
#       features = model.log2feats(sequence)[valid]
#       p = model.predict_score(features, positive[valid])
#       n = model.predict_score(features, negative_ids_K16)
#       target_losses, weights = bounded_masked_candidate_loss(
#           p, n, weighting_strength(epoch, E))
#       loss = audited_baseline_target_reduction(target_losses, target_rows)
#       Apply unchanged optimizer, schedule and clipping.
#     Apply unchanged host-compatible validation/checkpoint policy.
#   Save one selected checkpoint and emit the matching predictor.
# Preserve diagnostic APIs and report only measured diagnostics/host metrics.
# Inference: append MASK, left-pad, read greatest nonpadding index, score real IDs.
# Never combine separately trained checkpoints or predictions.

originality.positive: A bounded, normalized weighting curriculum gives a small, auditable BERT4Rec experiment using existing candidates and one scoring network.
originality.negative: Detached hardness weighting, normalization and warm starts are established techniques; experimental control contributes more than algorithmic novelty.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result can guide later investigations of hardness timing, extreme-negative suppression and semantic specificity within one BERT4Rec network.
future_potential.negative: The intervention addresses user complaints indirectly, and sampled-validation gains may not transfer to full-catalog usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The main implementation is a short loss function with no architecture or inference change.
code_difficulty.negative: Baseline integration, matched randomness, reduction auditing and trustworthy diagnostic reporting require care beyond the loss itself.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the bidirectional masked-item backbone and Cloze training foundation preserved by this proposal.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed bounded negative-weighting curriculum or its benchmark performance.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Motivates examining uncertain hard negatives and alternatives to unrestricted hardness emphasis.
limitations: Its collaborative-filtering setting does not establish gains for masked BERT4Rec or identify false negatives in these diagnostics.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-start and controlled introduction of harder training competition.
limitations: The proposed weighting schedule is an adaptation, not a reproduction of its sampling algorithm or evidence of BERT4Rec effectiveness.

related_work.title: NOVA-BERT
contributions: Motivates separating attention-guiding side information from item-ID value representations.
limitations: Does not validate the alternative scratch-trained title encoder under the supplied data and budget constraints.

related_work.title: TiSASRec
contributions: Provides a mechanism for incorporating pairwise time intervals into sequential attention.
limitations: Uses a different original backbone and does not establish a beneficial recency direction for this task.
